newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco expects 1.0 mln ha irrigated land in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Morocco expects 1.0 mln ha irrigated land in 96/97.

text.p: Morocco expects that by the end of the 1996/97 farming season the country would have 1.0 million hectares of land under irrigation, the Moroccan radio RTM said on Tuesday.

The radio quoted King Hassan II as saying on the 36th anniversary of his accession to the throne: "With a scheduled 93,000 hectares to be irrigated in the 1996/97 agricultural season...the target of 1.0 million hectares of irrigated lands will be met."
The king was quoted as adding this result was achieved thanks to "the policy of dams" launched by the authorities in the early 1960s.
Morocco has more than 60 medium and large dams of which half were built in the past 20 years, the radio said.

According to the agriculture ministry, a total of 5.6 million hectares are expected to be sown for all crops in the 1996/97 season, similar to the area for 1995/96. More than 900,000 hectares are located in irrigated areas, it added.
Morocco harvested a record 10 million tonnes of cereals last year, up from 1.6 million tonnes in 1995 when the country suffered a severe drought, the Statistics Directorate said.
The Casablanca-based think-tank Centre Marocain de Conjoncture, expects Morocco to produce 7.0 to 8.0 million tonnes of cereals in 1996/97 season, due to good rainfall during the winter.
